hypotheses.name: hL : NoLentAccess P
hypotheses.purpose: A lent local is neither read, assigned, nor borrowed until its borrow ends. The backward translation leaves a lent local at its old value until the borrow ends, while the reference semantics updates it in place, so a read of the lent local differs (cxLent).

hypotheses.name: hF : NoFrozenAccess P
hypotheses.purpose: A reborrowed borrow is not used until the reborrow ends. In the backward translation its current value is stale until the reborrow's backward function writes it back, while the reference semantics reads the shared address (cxFrozen).

hypotheses.name: hE : NoUseAfterEnd P
hypotheses.purpose: A borrow is not used after its end. In the backward translation a write after the end changes only the ended borrow's slot and is never written back, while the reference semantics performs it (cxAfterEnd).

hypotheses.name: hB : FreshBindings P
hypotheses.purpose: Every borrow-creating statement binds a name not bound before in its frame (syntactic single assignment of borrow names per frame). This also rejects reusing the name of a borrow that has already ended, which is stricter than forbidding the overwrite of a live borrow; on the example rebindEnded that reuse is harmless for both translations (rebindEnded_harmless). Rebinding a live name leaks that borrow, whose backward function is then never applied (cxRebind).

hypotheses.name: hX : AllEndedAtExit P
hypotheses.purpose: Every borrow of the main program has ended when the program ends. An unended borrow's backward function is never applied, so its lender keeps its old value, while the reference semantics has updated it in place (cxUnended).

depth_note: Requires a simulation invariant relating address-based states to backward states across nested reborrows, run-time selection, and calls (each call composing a callee summary).
